      "partial_result": "## Verdict: source GO once one small fd-leak fix lands\n\nI reproduced one real bug: it breaks the contract's \"close all descriptors on every failure\" rule, and the existing tests don't catch it. It isn't a safety problem, because the bad input is still rejected. Everything else I checked matches the reconciled contract. I didn't edit any source. Scratch falsifiers are in `/tmp/cie-falsify/` (stdlib only, \u226415 s, 1 GiB address space).\n\n### Bug 1 (must fix before freezing): a directory at a leaf path leaks one fd per rejected call\n\n- **Where:** `src/sfora/connected_installed_environment.py:356-357`. `os.open(name, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK)` succeeds on a directory. Then `os.fdopen(fd, \"rb\")` raises `IsADirectoryError`, and CPython does not close an fd it was handed. The `except OSError` turns this into `ValueError`, but only `directory` is closed in `finally`.\n- **Falsifier:** `/tmp/cie-falsify/f1_fd_leak.py`. It reuses the test's own setUp fixture and replaces `torch/__init__.py` with an empty directory.\n  - Python 3.12.13: **50 fds leaked after 50 rejected calls.**\n  - Python 3.14.4: also 50.\n  - FIFO control: 0 leaked. A missing leaf also opens no fd.\n- **Scope:** the same function reads every selected member, every RECORD and every METADATA file, so any of those paths being a directory triggers it.\n- **Minimal fix:** call `os.fstat(fd)` and check `S_ISREG` on the raw fd, closing it on failure, before wrapping it. Or skip `fdopen` and read with an `os.read` loop inside `try/finally: os.close(fd)`. Either way also stops `io.open` from running an `isatty()` ioctl on the leaf before the regular-file check.\n- **Missing test:** a leaf-directory case next to the FIFO/symlink/missing cases at `scripts/test_connected_installed_environment.py:284`, asserting that `/proc/self/fd` doesn't grow.\n\n### Missing evidence (fails closed; not a source bug)\n\nThe helper requires each selected and METADATA row to match exactly: path, canonical unpadded `sha256=` base64, and a canonical decimal size (`:404-409`, `:455-463`). The committed original collector only checked these rows loosely:\n- `complete-record-owner-collector.py:27-28` pads before `urlsafe_b64decode`, and that decoder silently drops non-alphabet characters.\n- Sizes only had to pass `isdigit()`, so leading zeros would pass.\n\nSo nothing committed proves the original RECORD rows are canonical. Because target RECORDs must byte-match the original SHA, one non-canonical original row would make every exact relocation fail. Normal pip/uv output is canonical, so this is probably fine. Today, though, the only check is the first real target run. `test_real_committed_correspondence\u2026` exercises only `_prepare`, never the RECORD row parse.\n\n### Optional hardening (no exposure with the pinned real inputs)\n\n- **Not fully strict JSON:** `json.loads(bytes)` accepts UTF-16, a UTF-8 BOM and lone-surrogate escapes (`f3_json_encoding.py` shows all three). The inputs are SHA-pinned to committed evidence, which is plain ASCII.\n- **Lexical vs. byte aliasing:** surrogate-escaped strings can name the same on-disk bytes as a different spelling, which would slip past the lexical root-overlap check. That only works when the original path has non-ASCII bytes. All 1,767 real paths, the 32 RECORD keys and the 1,754 row paths are ASCII, with no CSV-special characters. Rejecting paths that don't strictly encode as UTF-8 in `_path` would close it.\n- **Directory walk needs read permission:** it uses `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY` on each ancestor, so ancestors with execute-only permission are rejected. `O_PATH` would avoid that. This fails closed.\n- **Weak test coverage:** RECORD/METADATA leaf symlink, FIFO and directory cases, plus a symlink above the target root, all share one code path that's only tested through member leaves. Adding them is optional.\n\n### Checked and holding\n\n- **Pinned inputs:** both input SHAs are checked before either is parsed and before any target I/O. Inputs must be exactly `bytes`. JSON parsing rejects duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity and bools in count/size fields, and requires exact key sets. The audit's counts and pass flags carry no authority.\n- **Ownership and mapping:**\n  - One original root, derived from the six packages.\n  - Exact selected set, with no omission, duplicate or addition.\n  - The 13 anchors are all in `/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu`, are native-only and stay unread.\n  - Lexical separation holds between target, original root and anchor directories.\n  - Mapping has no collisions, and the full inverse round-trips with types and key order preserved.\n  - Package versions match their owners', and the constructor is selected.\n- **Reads:**\n  - Every step of the path walk is a `O_NOFOLLOW` descriptor, and the leaf is opened non-blocking.\n  - Size is checked before reading. Data is streamed in 1 MiB chunks with a 16 MiB cap for captured RECORD/METADATA. SHA and byte count come from the same fd.\n  - (dev, ino, size, mtime, ctime) must not change during the read.\n- **RECORD and METADATA:** the full RECORD SHA is checked before parsing. Exactly one exact selected row and one exact METADATA row are required. Name/Version must each appear once and match the audit. Unselected rows are never touched.\n- **No digest cache.** The 23 zero-byte real members are handled correctly.\n\nThe documented limits stay out of scope and are not bugs: global target ownership, import/pyc/pth, ISA (the original is CPython 3.13 on aarch64), RPATH and mapping, integrity after descriptors close, bind-mount aliasing, and the separate mandatory native gate for the anchors.
